hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation, attacked by hand on the real product (API, app database role, exports, headers)
hard_gates.evidence: api-attack.txt: tenant A (admin@alnoor) sees 44 of its own sequences and none of tenant B's 22. GET and PUT on B's sequence id return 404 and B's row is unchanged. Search and filter on B's company code or companyId return 0 rows. X-Tenant and X-Tenant-Id headers return 404. The CSV and PDF exports of the numbering list do not contain B's company code. db-attack-erp_app.txt: as erp_app with tenant A bound, B's sequences, counters and issued numbers are invisible and UPDATE affects 0 rows. A counter INSERT for B is refused by RLS, and an issued number pointing at B's sequence is refused by the composite (tenant_id, sequence_id) foreign key. RLS is enabled and forced on all three numbering tables, with tenant and company policies and the audit_capture trigger. I found no real leak.

hard_gates.gate: G1 HTTP isolation test inside ./erp verify (Tenant_A_cannot_reach_tenant_B_through_any_endpoint)
hard_gates.evidence: Run 1 (verify-kept/20261029T202658Z-8333/dotnet-suite.log:919-924, g1-http-failure-line.txt) failed with '1 answers that tell tenant B's values apart': GET /api/numbering/sequences?filter=nextNumber contains 'BQ-' (tenant B's prefix) returned 0 rows, but the random 'exists nowhere' control 'rv-' returned rows. Those rows were tenant A's own receipt vouchers (RV-{YYYY}-), because 'contains' ignores case. This is a false positive: the test treats a random control as non-existent, and here it matched A's own data. The same test passed in run 2 (20261030T005109Z-98606) and run 3 (20261030T050905Z-171706). It still failed on the real product, and p10's list of short two-letter prefixes is what makes the collision possible.

G2 suites passed in runs 2 and 3 (dotnet 814 of 814). By hand: viewer@alnoor can list (canUpdate false everywhere) and gets 403 on PUT. noaccess@alnoor gets 403 on list, get and PUT. Anonymous gets 401. In the browser the no-roles user has no menu entry, and the direct URL shows 'No access' (08-noaccess-direct-url.jpg). biggest_gap.title: The G1 HTTP isolation gate fails at random on p10's sequences list (false positive)
biggest_gap.detail: The differential check in G1HttpIsolationTests sends tenant B's value and a random 'value that exists nowhere' of the same shape. ControlFor(string) replaces each letter with a random lowercase letter, so B's prefix 'BQ-' becomes something like 'rv-'. p10's list filters nextNumber and prefix with a case-insensitive 'contains', and tenant A's own seeded sequences use two-letter prefixes (QT-, SO-, PO-, CN-, DN-, RV-, PV-, JV-). A random two-letter control therefore matches A's own rows about 1 time in 85 per attack, and the gate reports 'answers that tell tenant B's values apart' although nothing leaks. One run in three on this machine failed this way, which fails the whole suite and blocks every integration that includes p10. The fix has to keep the gate at least as strict, never loosen it. Options: choose a control that does not occur, case-insensitively, in the attacker's own unfiltered answer for that endpoint; or have p10's gate seed give tenant A prefixes that a random control of B's shape cannot hit, and document it. The differential machinery is p00's (done for now), so the owner or lead decides who changes it; the surface that triggers it is p10's. Builders also need a full verify that passes; on this machine the web stage only passed in quiet runs (see other findings).
biggest_gap.evidence: Run 1 kept folder verify-kept/20261029T202658Z-8333/dotnet-suite.log lines 919-924, also g1-http-failure-line.txt: 'GET /api/numbering/sequences?take=200&filter=nextNumber contains 'BQ-' [query filter]: 200 {"items":[],"total":0,...} but for a value that exists nowhere (rv-) 200 {"items":[{... "companyCode":"A1-CO","documentType":"payment...'. Control generator: tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G1/G1HttpIsolationTests.cs, ControlFor(string value), around line 1566 (random 'a'+n%26 per letter). The same test passed in runs 2 and 3 (verify-kept/20261030T005109Z-98606, 20261030T050905Z-171706). To reproduce: run ./erp verify a few times, or force ControlFor to return 'rv-' for 'BQ-'.

other_findings: Scope defect: switching a sequence from yearly to never and back to yearly in the same year leaves it stuck. The yearly counter keeps its old value, the preview shows a number already given, and every take fails with numbering.numberTaken, so no document of that type can be saved. On a gapless sequence the administrator also cannot set the next number (400 numberingGaplessNextNumberFixed); the only way out is to turn gapless off, set the number, and turn it back on. Repro: scripts/CriticProbeTests.cs, log probe-reset-toggle.log. Takes after yearly gave SX-202610-00001..3; after never, 00004..5; after yearly again the preview reads SX-202610-00004 and three takes are refused. Cause: SequenceEndpoints.Update carries the running counter over only when the new period's counter does not exist yet. No duplicate number was ever given, because the issued_numbers unique index holds.

Scope present and working: 11 document types per company (44 for Al Noor's four companies); prefix, suffix, padding 1-12, {YYYY} {YY} {MM} {BRANCH} tokens; never, yearly and monthly reset; gapless option (row lock in the caller's transaction, NULLS NOT DISTINCT counter key); per-branch counting; next-number override, never below a number already given; live preview of the next three numbers and the date the run starts again; issued numbers traced to SourceId; optimistic version check; audit_capture on all three tables.

Validation works in both languages: yearly without {YYYY}/{YY} and monthly without {MM} are refused with field messages, in English and Arabic (03-en-invalid-yearly.jpg, 06-ar-panel-validation.jpg). The leave guard appears on Escape with unsaved changes (04-en-leave-guard.jpg).

Arabic: dir=rtl lang=ar, every heading and label in Arabic, document numbers kept left to right inside Arabic sentences, no Latin words in the panel apart from the tokens (05-ar-list.jpg, walk-notes.txt). Keyboard: G then N reaches the screen, opening a row focuses and selects the prefix, Enter saves. No console errors.

Ours covers both on screen and I checked them by hand. A task variant with the reset would make the comparison complete (p01 is frozen, so this goes to the backlog).

human_gates.gate: Statutory rule (CLAUDE.md human gate: tax rules)
human_gates.what: Tax invoice and tax credit note numbering is governed by UAE VAT Executive Regulation Article 59(1): a sequential Tax Invoice number, or a unique number that identifies the invoice and its place in the sequence. p10 ships default patterns, reset and gapless settings for sales.invoice and sales.creditNote, and lets an administrator change them, including making them non-gapless or resetting them, with no rule recorded in docs/compliance/. The owner, with a senior accountant, should sign off which settings are allowed for tax documents, and the rule should be recorded with its source and check date.
